_note: ⛔ SNG-436. WORDING AUDIT — Erik: 'some of the skills read like they don't do ANYTHING.' ⚠️ CHECKED FIRST: skill_utility_audit.json (2026-07-07) already exists, but it audited TACTICAL utility across 106 skills — which challenge each answers — and concluded 'not more skills, PRESENTATION + a few reframes'. This is the PRESENTATION half, never done, now measured across all 376.
_finding:
⛔ 87 OF 376 DESCRIPTIONS OPEN BY DEFINING THE CRAFT RATHER THAN SAYING WHAT YOU DO. 'The mind-pole mastery:', 'The chaos-craft:', 'The Figurists' first offense:', 'The Masons' holding-craft.' ⚠️ THEY PLACE THE SKILL IN THE TRADITION'S TAXONOMY, WHICH IS A LIBRARIAN'S JOB, NOT A PLAYER'S QUESTION. The player is asking 'what happens when I use this?'
⛔ AND IT IS NOT A ROOT-ABILITY CONVENTION — I checked, because that would have made it legitimate: 46 of the 87 sit ABOVE levelReq 1, and mean level is 2.1 against 2.3 for the rest. The pattern is uncorrelated with tree position, so it is a habit rather than a rule.
⚠️ THE SAME TRADITION DOES BOTH, WHICH PROVES IT IS FIXABLE: Cogitant has 'Noesis — the mind-pole mastery: memory, focus, reason...' AND 'Cold-Read — infer another's thoughts and intent from micro-signals.' The second one tells you what you do.
_theRule:
⛔ A DESCRIPTION'S FIRST CLAUSE MUST NAME AN ACTION AND ITS OUTCOME. The taxonomy line is welcome AFTER that, never instead of it. Radiant Lance is the model: 'Focus light into a searing coherent beam — precise, silent, fast as sight.' ⚠️ Verb, object, result, then flavour.
⛔ WORST CASES FIRST: the 24 below define AND NEVER GET TO AN ACTION — no clause after the colon or dash. Those read as pure lore and are the ones Erik is hitting.
_layer1_generatedText: ⛔ SEPARATE AND CHEAPER: `plainly` is GENERATED from `mechanic` and the generator has grammar faults on 122 abilities. 64 'missing full stop before It' ('It rolls 1d6 It affects 1 target'), 46 'A' before a vowel sound ('A investigate/explore action'), 12 run-ons. ⚠️ THIS IS A CODE FIX, NOT CONTENT — one article rule and one join. It makes every skill read as sloppier than it is, and it is the FIRST thing a player sees under the name.

worstCases.name: The Whole Act
worstCases.description: The braid-craft: body and mind as one instrument, acting faster than either could decide — the Middle Way's ideal.
worstCases.narrationHints: Thought and motion stop being two things.

worstCases.name: The Sustained Regard
worstCases.description: The Cogitants' first offense. No vector, no contact, nothing crosses the space. Thought applied to a body that has been quietly running itself.
worstCases.narrationHints: You give them the whole of your attention and refuse to give it back. Under a regard that complete the body starts dropping the things it was doing unattended — balance, breath, the grip on a weapon, the clotting of a wound.

worstCases.name: Latticework
worstCases.description: The order-craft: structure, prediction, law, the binding of possibility. The Lattice-Cities' discipline — order as power.
worstCases.narrationHints: Structure imposed and possibility bound — a plan that holds, a prediction that lands, a binding that will not slip.

worstCases.name: The Sound Read
worstCases.description: The Masons' first craft, and the one they are actually hired for. Everything else they do rests on being right about this.
worstCases.narrationHints: You put a hand on a made thing and it tells you the truth about itself. Not a feeling about the stone — an answer: this member is bearing, that one is decorative, and the whole thing comes down from HERE.

worstCases.name: The Set Stone
worstCases.description: The Masons' holding-craft. Half of building is making a thing stay where you put it.
worstCases.narrationHints: You set a thing where it is and it STAYS. A stone, a beam, a door, a cart — placed with intent, it now takes far more than ordinary force to shift, and it will not drift, sag, settle or be quietly moved.

worstCases.name: Umbracraft
worstCases.description: The dark-pole mastery: concealment, sight-without-light, and the harboring of what should not be exposed. Not evil — the necessary shadow.
worstCases.narrationHints: The dark that hides and the dark that harbors — sight without light, the unseen made ally, the sheltering of what the blaze would burn.

worstCases.name: The Carried Dark
worstCases.description: The Umbrals' first craft. Not hiding IN shadow — carrying one.
worstCases.narrationHints: You bring the dark with you rather than finding it. A pocket of unlight that travels at your pace, and inside it you are simply not available to be seen.

worstCases.name: The Felt Room
worstCases.description: The Umbrals' seeing-craft, which is not seeing. It works best exactly where every other perception craft fails.
worstCases.narrationHints: In the lightless deeps you learn a place by everything except seeing — air movement, the way sound returns, the temperature of stone, the tiny wrongness of a room that has someone standing in it.

worstCases.name: The Hastened Grey
worstCases.description: The Ashwardens' first offense, and it is the tradition doing precisely what the tradition is for. Endings are their work. This is the work applied against someone.
worstCases.narrationHints: Everything is already ending. You put a hand on this one and bring it forward. A blade greys and shears; a strained rope parts; a wound that was closing opens grey at the edges and does not stop; a man who was going to die in forty years does it considerably sooner.

worstCases.name: The Kept Vigil
worstCases.description: The Ashwardens' keeping-craft, and the mirror of their hastening one. They tend endings, which means they also know precisely how to postpone one.
worstCases.narrationHints: You hold a thing at the edge it is already standing on. Not healing, not repair — HOLDING. The rope does not part, the wound does not turn, the truce does not break, for exactly as long as you attend it and no longer.

worstCases.name: The True Account
worstCases.description: The Ashwardens' seeing-craft. Everything is ending; the craft is knowing the schedule.
worstCases.narrationHints: You read what a thing has left. Not a feeling — a reckoning: what is wearing, how fast, and what it will fail from. Ashwardens are asked to look at bridges as often as at people.

worstCases.name: Descent
worstCases.description: The demonic-pole mastery: appetite named, bargains struck, the refusal to pretend that want is not the engine. Not evil — the honest hunger.
worstCases.narrationHints: Something in the room admits what it wants, and the admitting has teeth.

worstCases.name: Ascent
worstCases.description: The angelic-pole mastery: mercy given, judgment pronounced, the luminous certainty that both heals and terrifies. Not good in the flat sense — certainty is a danger.
worstCases.narrationHints: The light here does not warm. It measures.

worstCases.name: The Honest Price
worstCases.description: The Bargainers' making-craft, and the reason anyone sits at their table twice.
worstCases.narrationHints: You name what a thing will truly cost — to you, to them, to whoever is not in the room — and having named it, you can deliver it exactly. No trick is the trick. The Bargainers are trusted in the foothills because they are.

worstCases.name: The Given Way
worstCases.description: The Unmakers' opening-craft. The distinction from breaking in is the whole professional identity.
worstCases.narrationHints: Anything shut was shut by a method, and a method can be reversed. A lock, a seal, a bar, a knot, a bound working — it OPENS, undamaged, and can be shut again after by whoever is entitled to.

worstCases.name: The Quick Work
worstCases.description: The Wrights' first craft. A day's carpentry in a quarter of an hour, and it holds.
worstCases.narrationHints: You build the thing now, out of what is here, and it works. Not conjuring — building, at a speed that looks like cheating to anyone who has ever built anything.

worstCases.name: The Carried Name
worstCases.description: The Threnodists' keeping-craft. The dead are forgotten wrong before they are forgotten entirely, and this is the answer to the first part.
worstCases.narrationHints: You hold a dead person's name the way a room holds a struck bell. Speak it and what they were comes back into the space — not a ghost, a WEIGHT. People remember correctly for as long as you hold it.

worstCases.name: The Shared Weight
worstCases.description: The Threnodists' mercy, and it is a real one because it is not free. Grief-singers are the people who will hold your share.
worstCases.narrationHints: You take part of what someone is carrying and carry it yourself. Not comfort — TRANSFER. They can stand up because some of it is on you now.

worstCases.name: The Plain Seeing
worstCases.description: The Verists' first craft and the one every other Verist craft rests on. You cannot say the true thing until you can see it.
worstCases.narrationHints: You look at a thing and what is actually so about it is simply available. Not detection, not deduction — the removal of everything that was in the way, including what you were hoping.

worstCases.name: The Kept Count
worstCases.description: The Hourkeepers' first craft and the reason valleys keep one. Everyone else estimates.
worstCases.narrationHints: You know how long. Not a guess — a count. How long the food lasts, how long before they arrive, how long this fever runs, how long you have been standing here thinking it was a moment.

worstCases.name: The Stretched Hour
worstCases.description: The Hourkeepers' giving-craft, and the one they are begged for. It is the exact inverse of the Spent Hour and costs the same in the other direction.
worstCases.narrationHints: You give a thing more time than it has. The lamp burns an hour longer on the same oil; the poultice holds through the night; the food does not turn; the dying man gets until morning. Time added, not conjured — and taken from somewhere.

worstCases.name: The Edge
worstCases.description: The violence-pole mastery: the martial disciplines honed to an art. Not fury — force made exact.
worstCases.narrationHints: Violence as a discipline, not a rage — economical, decisive, terrible in its precision. The Marchers do not brawl; they end.

worstCases.name: The Held Breath
worstCases.description: The braid-craft: hold a moment where violence is total and peace is total in perfect tension — an armed grace.
worstCases.narrationHints: Violence and peace both at a knife's edge, held by will alone.

worstCases.name: The Read Field
worstCases.description: The Marchers' seeing-craft. The March holds because it chose the ground before anyone arrived.
worstCases.narrationHints: You look at ground and see the fight it will produce — where a charge must funnel, where a line will break first, which approach a sensible enemy takes and which a frightened one does.
